header.title: Getting started
header.description: Install Gemsitions, load the styles and animate how your UI enters, exits and changes with React transitions.

peers.title: Peers
peers.body: React 19. @gem-org/gem-system is optional: when it is installed, transitions read its tokens (--gem-*); otherwise they use neutral values. Gemsitions does not reimplement design-system components.

usage.title: Basic usage
usage.description: Each transition wraps its child and is driven by `isIn`. With `isIn` set to `false` it animates the exit and unmounts the content when it ends.

bootstrap.title: Bootstrap
bootstrap.description: The fastest path: import styles.css once in your entry point and use the transitions from the barrel.

partial.title: Import only what you need
partial.description: Each transition ships as its own subpath (kebab-case, for example @gem-org/gemsitions/fade-transition) with a matching stylesheet (fade-transition.css). That way the bundle only includes the JS and CSS of the transitions you actually use.
partial.label: Partial import

notes.tokens: Import tokens.css once: it defines the --gemst-* duration, easing and intensity variables.
notes.utilities: utilities.css is optional: it adds layout, overflow and position classes (gemst-relative, gemst-overflow-hidden…) to pass through className or classNames.
notes.utils: Motion helpers (usePresenceTransition, prefersReducedMotion…) live in @gem-org/gemsitions/utils and tokens in @gem-org/gemsitions/tokens.
notes.single: Pick one path: styles.css already includes tokens, utilities and every transition, so do not mix it with individual imports.

behavior.title: Shared behavior
behavior.description: Most transitions share the same API, so what you learn with one applies to the rest.

items.timing: Timing: duration, delay and easing. All three accept a single value or { enter, exit }; easing accepts a token (standard, enter, exit, emphasized, linear) or any CSS timing function.
items.presence: Presence (Fade, Slide, Scale and Collapse): keepMounted keeps the node hidden in the DOM, initial={false} skips the first-mount animation and onPhaseChange reports every phase (entering, entered, exiting, exited).
items.phases: Events: every transition emits on* when it enters and out* when it exits (onFade / outFade), with a reason: enter, exit, inactive, disabled or unmount.
items.classes: Styling: className, style and per-slot classNames. Public classes use the .gemst-* prefix (BEM) and variables use --gemst-*.

asChild.title: asChild
asChild.description: With `asChild` the transition does not add a `div`: it merges its classes, styles and ref into the single child. Use it inside Flex or Grid, or on a real semantic element. The child must be exactly one React element.

tokens.title: Motion tokens
tokens.description: Gemsitions owns duration, easing and intensity. Palette, type, spacing and radius come from the host app (--gem-*).
tokens.intensity: Durations go from `instant` (`0ms`) to `slower` (`1000ms`); intensity accepts a token (`sm`, `md` or `lg`, equal to 35%, 55% and 80%) or a number between `0` and `1`.

a11y.title: Reduced motion
a11y.description: Transitions support interface changes; content must make sense without motion too.

items.reducedMotion: Every transition honors prefers-reduced-motion: reduce: motion snaps straight to the final state.
items.ignore: Use ignoreReducedMotion (it adds the gemst-ignore-reduced-motion class) only when motion is essential to the experience.
items.properties: Transitions animate transform and opacity whenever possible, to avoid forcing reflows.
items.viewTransition: ViewTransition uses document.startViewTransition() and applies a CSS fallback when the browser lacks the API.
